hook.text: Heat isn't a substance—it's the random motion of trillions of atoms jostling and vibrating.

buildup.text: Temperature measures the average kinetic energy of particles—hotter means faster molecular motion.

discovery.text: Heat always flows from hot to cold—never the reverse, unless you spend energy to force it (like a refrigerator).

twist.text: The ocean stores more thermal energy than all fossil fuel reserves combined—but it's too diffuse to easily extract.

climax.text: Rubbing your hands creates heat through friction—kinetic energy converts directly into thermal energy.

punchline.text: Heat is atoms in a hurry—going nowhere in particular.

quiz.question: What does temperature measure?
options: How much work an object can do
